---
title: "R Packages Setup"
---

Welcome! To make the most of the **Spatiotemporal Modelling Workshop**, you must have your computing environment configured *before* we begin on Monday morning. These models (VAST, sdmTMB) are computationally intensive and rely on a specific stack of C++ compilers and spatial libraries.

## Computing Requirements

You will need:
  
  * **A laptop with administrative privileges:** Necessary to install C++ compilers and Rtools.
* **Secondary monitor:** Highly recommended so you can follow the live-coding demonstrations while keeping your own RStudio session open.
* **R and RStudio:** Ensure you have the latest versions installed.
* **C++ Toolchain:** Necessary for **TMB** (Template Model Builder) to compile the spatiotemporal models.
* **Git & GitHub:** For collaborative code sharing and version control.


---

## 1. Install R and RStudio (if necessary)

We rely on recent features for spatial data handling (`sf`, `terra`).
* **R:** Version **>= 4.4.0** (4.5 recommended) - Download from [cloud.r-project.org](https://cloud.r-project.org/).
* **RStudio:** Desktop version **>= 2025.09** - Download from [posit.co](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/).

---


## 2. Install Core R Packages
Open RStudio and run this script to install the engine and the diagnostic tools.

```r
# 1. Install CRAN dependencies
install.packages(c("devtools", "sdmTMB", "DHARMa", "sf", "terra", "ggplot2", 
                   "units", "remotes", "fmesher", "TMB", "Rcpp"))

# 2. Install VAST (and its dependency FishStatsUtils)
# Install and load devtools package
#install.packages("devtools")
library("devtools")

# Install package
install_github("james-thorson/VAST@main", INSTALL_opts="--no-staged-install")
# Load package
library(VAST)

#If you are having problems with installation, please consider installing dependencies individually, e.g. using:

# Install TMB from CRAN
install.packages("TMB")

# Install INLA using currently recommended method
install.packages("INLA", repos=c(getOption("repos"), INLA="https://inla.r-inla-download.org/R/stable"), dep=TRUE)

# Install FishStatsUtils from CRAN
install_github("james-thorson/FishStatsUtils@main", INSTALL_opts="--no-staged-install")


# 3. Install sdmTMB
#sdmTMB can be installed from CRAN:
install.packages("sdmTMB", dependencies = TRUE)

#Assuming you have a C++ compiler installed, the development version is recommended and can be installed:
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("sdmTMB/sdmTMB", dependencies = TRUE)


# 4. Install tinyVAST
# The bridge between sdmTMB flexibility and VAST multivariate power

#tinyVAST can be installed from CRAN:
install.packages("tinyVAST")

#or the dev branch (subject to ongoing changes) can be installed from GitHub:
library(devtools)
install_github("vast-lib/tinyVAST", dependencies = TRUE)
```

---

## 3. Data Preparation Checklist
To participate in the **"Bring Your Own Data"** sessions, please have a clean dataset ready with the following columns:

- [ ] **Year** (Numeric integer)
- [ ] **Latitude / Longitude** (Decimal degrees)
- [ ] **Response Variable** (Biomass, Counts, or CPUE)
- [ ] **Effort** (Area swept, tow duration, or number of hooks)
- [ ] **Vessel/Gear ID** (Factor, for standardization)

::: {.callout-tip}
## Spatial Unit Warning
VAST and sdmTMB perform best when spatial coordinates are **Projected** (e.g., UTM in kilometers). If you only have Lat/Lon, we will cover how to project them on Day 1, but having an idea of your area's UTM zone is a plus!
:::

---

## Troubleshooting
If you encounter errors during the installation of `VAST` or `TMB`:
1. Restart RStudio.
2. Ensure no other R sessions are running.
3. If a prompt asks *"Do you want to install from sources?"*, type **Yes**.

For urgent support, contact **Sosthene AKIA** via email.
